Q3587190.label: 2011 Jamaican general election
Q3587190.summary: General elections were held in Jamaica on 29 December 2011. The elections were contested mainly between the nation's two major political parties, the governing Jamaica Labour Party (JLP), led by Andrew Holness, and the Portia Simpson-Miller-led opposition People's National Party (PNP).

Q6543990.label: 1928 Liechtenstein general election
Q6543990.summary: General elections were held in Liechtenstein on 15 and 29 July 1928 to elect the 15 members of the Landtag. Early elections had been called due to Johann II, Prince of Liechtenstein, forcing the resignation of the Christian-Social People's Party (VP) led government of prime minister Gustav Schädler due to an embezzlement scandal. The Progressive Citizens' Party (FBP) won a majority of eleven seats, whereas the VP won four. Voter turnout was 93.1%.

Q296054.label: Klement Gottwald

He was the first leader of Communist Czechoslovakia from 1948 to 1953.

Q2069110.label: 1976 Maltese general election

Q1568374.label: Wye River Memorandum
Q1568374.desc: 1998 step in the Israel-Palestinian peace process
Q1568374.summary: The Wye River Memorandum was an agreement negotiated between Israel and the Palestinian Authority at a summit in Wye River, Maryland, U.S., held 15–23 October 1998. Q98380406.label: Marjorie Taylor Greene
Q98380406.summary: Marjorie Taylor Greene, also known by her initials MTG, is an American politician, businesswoman, and conspiracy theorist who served as the U.S. representative for Georgia's 14th congressional district from 2021 until her resignation in 2026. A former member of the Republican Party, she was elected to Congress in 2020 following the retirement of Republican incumbent Tom Graves and was reelected in 2022 and 2024. Greene is widely considered to be a populist and far-right politician.

Q1470070.label: Ploughmen's Front
Q1470070.summary: The Ploughmen's Front was a Romanian left-wing agrarian-inspired political organisation of ploughmen, founded at Deva in 1933 and led by Petru Groza. At its peak in 1946, the Front had over 1 million members.
